title: Degrees of coverage
core: All four say nothing was left out — but they answer different questions: *left out of what?* One measures a job done properly, one measures a finite set of cases run to the end, one measures a whole subject held in someone's head, one measures a scope with no visible edges. The scale runs from a task you can finish to a totality you can only gesture at. As the scope widens, the claim gets grander and the risk of overkill or suffocation grows with it.

words.nuance: The only one that praises **effort rather than reach** — it certifies the worker, not the size of the field. A thorough search covers the house; it makes no claim that every house was searched. It's also the only member with a second life as a pre-noun intensifier, and there it turns hostile: *a thorough nuisance*, *a thorough scoundrel*.

The claim shifts from diligence to **arithmetic: the set is finite and it is now finished** — every file, every name, every possibility. You can be thorough on an open-ended problem; you can only be **exhaustive** where the cases can be counted off. Its shadow is proportion: exhaustive on a trivial question is tedium.

Widens from a task to **an entire subject domain**, and almost always lands on a person's knowledge or memory rather than a search or a study. It buys **breadth plus instant recall, never insight** — the encyclopedic scholar may have no argument at all. Aim it at a book or a style and the compliment dies: catalogue-flat, everything listed, nothing said.

Drops the checklist entirely — there is no enumerable set here, just **something with no edges**, so it attaches to abstractions: a theory, a vision, a grief, a love. It carries awe where the others carry competence. Turn it on a feeling and the awe curdles into confinement: an all-encompassing obsession leaves room for nothing else.

exam_note: Watch for **exhaustive/exhausting** swapped in a completion, and for **encyclopedic** offered where the sentence actually praises depth or originality — it only ever certifies breadth.
